steps.title: Prepare brain tissue sections
steps.instruction: Use 40 µm thick sections from saline‑perfused C57BL/6 mice (Jackson Labs, cat #00064) that have been fixed in 4 % paraformaldehyde for 24 h, cryopreserved in 30 % sucrose, and harvested seven weeks after distal middle cerebral artery occlusion.

steps.title: Wash sections in PBS
steps.instruction: Place each section in a well of a 12‑well tissue‑culture plate and wash three times for 10 min each in 0.1 M PBS at room temperature on a shaker.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Block for 1 h at room temperature with 10 % goat serum and 0.3 % Triton X‑100 in 0.1 M PBS (use serum from the species that generated the secondary antibody).

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Incubate sections overnight at room temperature on a rotator in 3 % goat serum + 0.3 % Triton X‑100 in 0.1 M PBS containing rat anti‑CD68 (1 : 500) and rabbit anti‑Iba1 (1 : 500). If staining is faint, increase antibody concentration or extend incubation to 48–72 h; if background is high, reduce concentration (recommended 1 : 500–1 : 1000).

steps.title: Wash after primary
steps.instruction: Wash three times for 10 min each in 0.1 M PBS at room temperature on a shaker.

steps.title: Incubate with secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Incubate for 2 h at room temperature in 3 % goat serum + 0.3 % Triton X‑100 in 0.1 M PBS with goat anti‑rabbit (1 : 500) and goat anti‑rat (1 : 500). Adjust concentration or extend to 4 h if staining is faint or background is high (recommended 1 : 500–1 : 1000). Keep samples protected from light from this point onward.

steps.title: Wash after secondary (light‑protected)
steps.instruction: Wash three times for 10 min each in 0.1 M PBS at room temperature on a shaker, keeping samples protected from light.

steps.title: Mount sections on slides
steps.instruction: Gently transfer sections to 0.1 M PBS, place them on Superfrost Plus microscope slides, air‑dry for ~30 min (do not exceed 1 h), and draw a hydrophobic barrier around each section with a pap‑pen.

steps.title: First PBS wash before BODIPY
steps.instruction: Wash the sections three times for 10 min each in 0.1 M PBS at room temperature.

steps.title: Stain with BODIPY
steps.instruction: Incubate sections in a solution of BODIPY 493/503 diluted 1 : 25 in DMSO for 30 min, protected from light.

steps.title: Second PBS wash
steps.instruction: Wash the sections three times for 10 min each in 0.1 M PBS at room temperature, protected from light.

steps.title: Apply antifade mounting medium
steps.instruction: Mount sections with antifade mounting medium, cover‑slip, and incubate 1–2 h at room temperature protected from light.

steps.title: Image fluorescence
steps.instruction: Acquire images on a fluorescence microscope using a 493 nm excitation filter and a 503 nm emission filter to detect BODIPY‑stained lipid droplets.

description: Validation of protocol Autofluorescence control Background: Autofluorescence, predominantly from lipofuscin, presents a significant challenge for researchers studying injured and diseased brain tissue, as it occurs across a spectrum from 480 to 695 nm [5]. It can be observed by imaging an unstained section through multiple filter cubes with different excitation and emission settings. Lipofuscin autofluorescence is most intense at lower wavelengths and gradually diminishes as wavelengths increase, necessitating longer exposure times for accurate capture ( Figure 1A –D). Considering that the BODIPY 493/503 stain emits at 503 nm, it is crucial to ensure that the stained areas accurately represent lipids in the brain rather than artifacts from lipofuscin autofluorescence. Figure 1. The broad spectrum of lipofuscin autofluorescence. A. Lipofuscin-rich infarcted region of a brain section from a stroked mouse, imaged with an exposure time of 1.2 s, excitation of 355–425 nm, and emission of 470 nm. B. The same section imaged with an exposure time of 1.2 s, excitation of 460–500 nm, and emission of 512–542 nm. C. The same section imaged with an increased exposure time of 3 s, excitation of 540–580 nm, and emission of 590–650 nm. D. The same section imaged with an increased exposure time of 10 s, excitation of 590–650 nm, and emission of 662–738 nm. All images were captured at 10× magnification with the scale bar representing 300 µm. Experimental setup: To address the issue of autofluorescence, we conducted a control experiment using two brain tissue samples from the same experimental group. One sample was stained with BODIPY according to the described protocol while the other was only incubated in PBS for the same duration instead of the BODIPY solution. Both samples were imaged using a Leica microscope the following day.
